Formal Product Safety Complaint  Samsung Appliances
[REDACTED]
Date: 05/19/2025

To Whom It May Concern,
I am submitting this incident report to formally document two separate, unresolved product defects involving Samsung appliances sold through BrandsMart USA. Both cases involve long-standing manufacturer-related failures that have led to unaddressed safety risks, denied service, and unresolved consumer loss.

This report is being submitted to Samsung Corporate Escalation and BrandsMart USA Executive Services, and a copy is being sent to the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) for review and regulatory purposes.
1. Samsung Gas Range  Gas Leak & Unsafe Defect (Independent of Fire)
Model: NX60A6751SS/AA
Serial Number: 0JE57DAX100725
Incident Summary:
A cooking fire occurred in 2024 on the left-front burner of this unit. I accept full responsibility for that event and am not requesting warranty coverage for fire damage. However, after the fire, a persistent gas leak was discovered coming from the front-right burner, which was not involved in the fire.

Upon closer inspection, it was discovered that this burner's control knob was bent at delivery. I initially assumed the bend was cosmetic and not safety-related, as there were no warnings, documentation, or guidance to indicate otherwise.

Following the fire, I began smelling gas regularly in the kitchen, specifically from the right side of the range. I reported this to Samsung, and a technician was dispatched on August 23, 2024. The technician confirmed that:
- The gas leak was real, and
- The leak originated from the bent knob and its associated gas valve or burner cup, not from the side that experienced fire.

Despite this technician-confirmed defect, my complaint was denied. BrandsMarts office manager verbally informed me that the entire unit was voided of coverage due to the fire, and no effort was made by either party to address the independent gas leak.

I have lived in this home with a gas leak for months, unaware of the risk. As a full-time student, I could not afford private repairs. Despite clear evidence that the bent knob was a manufacturer-originating defect, no remedy was offered, and my safety concern remains unaddressed.
[REDACTED]
